# The ERROR-ORIGIN INVENTORY: every place the SDK's .vis surface tells someone that something went wrong.
#
#   file <TAB> shape <TAB> count <TAB> family <TAB> classification
#
# SCOPE is the .vis engine plus ProjectAppService -- the surface the coded-problem mechanism migrates first.
# The controller API tier (controllerService, labservice, internalTestService) is deliberately outside it: it
# is a separate surface with its own outcomes, and pulling it in would have made this inventory a survey
# rather than a checklist.
#
# CLASSIFICATION, per invariant 10, and it is the whole point of the artifact:
#   Refusal  -- the user is told, in Danish, that an operation will not be carried out. Needs a CODE.
#   Failure  -- something broke; the English diagnostic goes to the log and a fixed Danish label goes to the
#               user. Needs no code of its own beyond the catch-all.
#   Finding  -- a report about a file's content rather than about an operation. Already coded.
#
# ARGUMENT guards are excluded by design. A public method called with an out-of-contract argument is a
# programming error, not an outcome a user can act on, and there are ~100 of them; coding them would put a
# Danish sentence in front of an installer for a bug in a caller.
#
# COUNTS are what make this a gate rather than a list: a new origin changes a count and fails the fitness
# test, so an uncoded refusal cannot be added quietly. Regenerate deliberately, and only when the new origin
# has been classified.
